title: kbmon host panel: load, whole-suite and main lock holders, suite ceiling status, read-only
goal: the host panel of kbmon.py shows the 1, 5 and 15 minute load with the core count, the whole-suite lock's holder pid with this clone or another and its start, the main lock's holder and step and the suite's ids, files and last full-run seconds against the numbers of _tools/tests_ceiling.json, read through tests.py's and kg_lock's readers; a host with no os.getloadavg shows the load as unsupported and the rest as on other hosts

clauses.clause: the host panel of kbmon.py shows the 1, 5 and 15 minute load with the core count, the whole-suite lock's holder pid with this clone or another and its start, the main lock's holder and step and the suite's ids, files and last full-run seconds against the numbers of _tools/tests_ceiling.json, read through tests.py's and kg_lock's readers

the host panel of kbmon.py shows the 1, 5 and 15 minute load with the core count, the whole-suite lock's holder pid with this clone or another and its start, the main lock's holder and step and the suite's ids, files and last full-run seconds against the numbers of _tools/tests_ceiling.json, read through tests.py's and kg_lock's readers

gates.question: How does the host panel name the clone a lock holder runs in, given that no path outside the clone is shown?
gates.host_unchecked: a design choice of how the panel words a clone; no host setup to prove

gates.question: Where does the host panel read the suite's ids and the last full-run seconds?
options: the newest passing full test.run row of the ops rows
collect the ids with pytest and time nothing
gates.recommendation: the newest passing full test.run row of the ops rows
gates.answer: the newest passing full test.run row of the ops rows

gates.question: How does the host panel colour a ceiling bar, given the view colours whole rows only?
options: a gutter flag: yellow from 80%, red from 100%, no colour under 80%
extend mon_view to colour a bar's run, green under 80%
gates.recommendation: a gutter flag: yellow from 80%, red from 100%, no colour under 80%
gates.answer: a gutter flag: yellow from 80%, red from 100%, no colour under 80%

gates.question: What does the host panel show for a lock file whose holder pid no longer runs?
How does the host panel lay out the three ceiling bars (ids, files, last run) by width?
options: one shared row from 100 columns, coloured by the worst bar, else three aligned rows
always three aligned rows, each with its own colour
gates.recommendation: one shared row from 100 columns, coloured by the worst bar, else three aligned rows
gates.answer: one shared row from 100 columns, coloured by the worst bar, else three aligned rows

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: read-only on _tools/tests_ceiling.json and the lock files: the panel imports tests and kg_lock and changes neither (tests.py is an agents-rule path). kb: os.getloadavg is documented for Unix only (python/stdlib-os-loadavg.md:22, DOC S-ew7mucsg). Data: load [1,5,15] or unsupported, cores, suite_lock {pid, clone, started} or null, main_lock {pid, step, clone} or null, ceiling {max_ids, max_files, max_seconds, ids, files, last_run_s}. Layout of the host panel (operator's spec): load (1/5/15 · cores) · locks (suite pid · this clone or another · since; main lock or none) · ceiling: ids, files and last full run, each `{used}/{limit} [|||||||||.] {pct}%` with 10 cells, green under 80%, yellow 80-99%, red at 100% or more; under 100 columns the three as aligned rows.
